statement: Intel's CEO said on the company's earnings call that demand for EMIB-T packaging remains very high with a growing backlog, and that Intel is targeting high-volume production and supporting customer ramps in 2027.
why: A growing packaging backlog at a second supplier signals real capacity being added outside the incumbent CoWoS route, which is the tightest link in the accelerator supply chain.

impact.mechanism: Rising bookings and a 2027 high-volume ramp at an alternative advanced-packaging supplier add capacity that competes with CoWoS and relieves the packaging bottleneck on accelerator output.

evidence.excerpt: high-volume production and supporting customer ramps in 2027

confidence.basis: Management commentary from an Intel earnings call reaching us through a secondary aggregator quoting a transcript service; qualitative, with no backlog figure disclosed.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> rising); sources: TrendForce
